_comment: The practice sources for this document project. A shared repository
declares universal and team sources ONLY -- an individual set belongs
in that person's own user-level config, never here, so its existence
and location aren't visible to everyone else on the project. See
tools/precedent_resolve.py for the resolution and precedence rules.
The universal source is a real vendored copy at the path below --
INSTALL.md §0 step 1 -- not a live reference; every collaborator and
every fresh container needs it without a sibling checkout.
TWO team sources, each named for a SUBJECT rather than for a roster,
and a project declares the ones its kind of work needs (INSTALL.md's
'Which team sets does this repo declare?'):
precedent-team-writing -- the craft of documents and prose: length,
emphasis, lists, drafting markers, citation and linking. Wanted by
anyone writing for a human reader, on any team.
precedent-team-working-style -- how a session works alongside the
person: decide small calls, don't stall on a non-blocking question,
don't repeat the same disclaimer every run. Mostly resident, so it
fires on every turn.
precedent-team-tms was declared here until 2026-09-10 and is RETIRED.
It held exactly one practice, `audience-register`, which moved to
precedent-team-working-style -- its subject is how a session talks to
the person, not this team's documents, and the file said so itself.
The move keeps the rule's whole point intact: it exists to override a
same-slug INDIVIDUAL practice asking for a more technical register,
and precedence is by LEVEL (team > repo-local > individual >
universal), so any team set outranks the individual one. A set that
was built for an editorial pilot nobody started, and that no repo
ever declared in anger, is a source a session has to resolve for
nothing.
precedent-team-maintainers is deliberately NOT declared here: it holds
repo and practice-set mechanics -- syncs, gates, branch setup, catalogue
upkeep -- which a document project has no way to act on. Not declaring a
set is the cheap way to say that; a `not_binding` entry per slug is the
expensive one. (Until 2026-09-09 this comment called that set 'code-repo
conventions', which was never true: over half its rules were about
writing, and they were unreachable from here because of it.)
Both are resolved LIVE from sibling clones, never vendored, per
those sources' own precedence rules. A hosted/ephemeral session needs
AGENTS.md's own instruction to call add_repo for each at session start
-- that instruction reads this file's `sources` rather than naming any
set, so declaring another one here is the only edit required.
_visibility_comment: PRIVATE, and this field is not optional for this template.
build_views.repo_is_public() reads a precedent.json that omits
`visibility` as PUBLIC -- deliberately, because the two ways of
being wrong are not symmetric and an undeclared field is exactly
how a public repo publishes somebody's private practice text by
accident. The cost of that safe default lands here: a PUBLIC repo
has team- and individual-level practice text excluded from
everything tracked, so a project instantiated from this template
into the private repository its own README step 1 tells you to
create would materialize the universal set ALONE and bind none of
the three team sets this template exists to wire in.
That is what happened. Instantiated verbatim, with this field
absent, a real install materialized 89 practices instead of 121
and the three team sources bound nothing -- and it looked like a
successful install, because the only signal was one NOTICE line
that read as informational (2026-09-10, installing
precedent-beta-v01 into a real project).
A project instantiated into a genuinely PUBLIC repository should
change this to "public" and understand what it is choosing: the
team sets stay in force for a session, but their text is carried
out of band (see tools/precedent_session_practices.py) rather
than committed. Do not simply delete the field -- an omission
reads as "public" too, but silently and without the choice.

not_binding.reason: Governs landing practices in bulk into a catalogue. This project consumes a catalogue and holds none of its own; the practices it captures go to precedent-team-writing, where this rule is in force.
A sweep of every source's full catalogue. This project owns no catalogue to sweep; the audit belongs to whoever maintains precedent-team-writing and the universal set.
Reads every practice repo in force against itself, pass by pass. That is maintenance of the practice system, not of a document project's own work.
Checks whether the practices that should have fired for recent work actually fired -- an audit of the catalogue's routing, run where the catalogue lives.
Vendoring an upstream practice layer and checking improvements back in. This project vendors the engine but does not maintain it, and contributes practices through precedent-team-writing instead.
Rolling a change out to attached team, individual or repo-local sources. This project attaches no source it is responsible for keeping in step.
Exporting a tool across a repo boundary. This project exports no tooling; it receives a vendored engine.
Applies to a repo migrating off an older practice system onto Precedent. A project instantiated from this template starts on Precedent, so there is no prior vocabulary to scrub.
Fixes the name of a repository that holds practices, by level. Binds whoever declares or creates a source; a project instantiated from this template has its sources chosen for it and creates none.
Guards the vendored, publicly-exported tree so it is public-safe at all times. This project publishes nothing upstream and has no such tree.
Requires citing a practice's slug in a code comment where the code is. This project produces documents, not code.
Requires a script to assert its own properties and the anchors a document cites from it. This project writes no scripts.
Requires computed content to live in a sync-gated generated block produced by a script. Figures here are written and checked by people, not computed.
Requires every script-derived figure to sit inside a generated block. Nothing here derives figures from a script.

Requires attempting a mechanical check before leaving a new rule advisory-only. The people who write rules here cannot write checks; the attempt belongs with precedent-team-writing's maintainers, and this project's rules reach them as candidates.
Promotes a costly broken convention to a script that exits non-zero. Same reason as checkable-gets-checked: writing that script is not work this project can do.
Governs a build-versus-buy decision on a software component, decomposed part by part. This project builds no software.

_not_binding_comment: Which universal practices are IN FORCE at their source but do NOT bind a
document project. Every entry carries a mandatory reason --
an exemption nobody argued for is the same silence this mechanism replaces.
Why this list exists at all: this template declares the full universal
catalogue alongside its declared team sets, and
materialization flattens both, so without these entries an editorial
project receives every rule about running a code repository. Found
2026-09-07 by the very deep check. The right correction is to exempt what
was never about this work, with a reason -- NOT to soften rules for
everyone, which would cost technical adopters the loudness that works.
DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE. Exempted here are only practices that are
clearly about maintaining the practice system itself, or that require
writing and running code. Anything arguable is left BINDING on purpose:
a rule that binds unnecessarily is noise a reader can skip, while a rule
wrongly exempted is a gap nobody sees. Err toward binding. Several
borderline ones were left in force on exactly that reasoning --
two-check-levels, session-bootstrap, pr-template-honest-gates,
no-rewrite-for-warnings, tabular-shared-renderer, one-formatter-per-quantity
and generated-artifact-provenance among them -- and a project that finds
one of them genuinely inapplicable should add it here with its own reason.
An entry naming a slug nothing puts in force is reported as stale, and a
`severity: blocking` practice cannot be exempted at all. Neither bites
here: all 66 are exemptible (the only blocking practice in Precedent is
repo-local to BestPractice and is not in this project's resolved set).
